themes.name: Assessment of ESD Effectiveness
themes.definition: The evaluation and measurement of how effectively Education for Sustainable Development is implemented, often focusing on students' knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, or competencies, using methods such as surveys, questionnaires, and structural equation modeling.
evidence: [ValMet_2020] This paper presents a methodology to evaluate (1) to what extent students of a higher degree in the field of education acquire sustainability competencies, and (2) to determine whether the subjects that develop Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) achieve their learning objectives.
[CheAss_2025] This study was conducted among students of Tibet University to assess their levels of knowledge, attitudes and behaviours related to sustainable development.

themes.name: Educator Professional Development in ESD
themes.definition: Programs and initiatives aimed at training university teachers and academic staff to integrate sustainability into their teaching and curricula, often involving workshops, training sessions, and pedagogical tools to enhance their professional competence.
evidence: [BiaEdu_2018] The purpose of this paper is to present a professional development experience for higher education academic staff within the framework of an international Tempus project focused on reorienting university curricula to address sustainability.
[HemESD_2024] This paper aims to analyze the extent to which education for sustainable development (ESD) training enhances university teachers’ professional competence.

themes.name: Curriculum Integration of Sustainability
themes.definition: The process of revising and incorporating sustainable development principles into university courses and curricula, often through reorienting existing programs or developing new ones to address sustainability challenges.
evidence: [BiaEdu_2018] revising curricula to phase sustainable development principles into university courses.
[CavPro_2021] examining the level of ESD, as input affecting the business programs curricula of the universities concerned.

themes.name: Pedagogical Innovations for ESD
themes.definition: The adoption of new and effective teaching methods to foster sustainability learning, such as design-thinking, project-based learning, experiential learning, or thematic approaches, aimed at enhancing student engagement and cognitive performance.
evidence: [HuaTo _2024] thematic teaching and design-thinking strategies were applied to these respective groups.
[GalInq_2021] a project work methodology proposed to students, based on an inquiry perspective.

themes.name: Institutional Strategies for ESD Implementation
themes.definition: Approaches and policies at the institutional level to mainstream and implement Education for Sustainable Development across higher education institutions, including monitoring, policy alignment, and strategic planning.
evidence: [HolMon_2024] monitoring SDG 4.7: Assessing Education for Sustainable Development in policies, curricula, training of educators and student assessment.
[SyeNar_2023] four prevailing approaches to implementing education for sustainable development at Malaysian higher education institutions.

themes.name: Interdisciplinary and Transdisciplinary Approaches
themes.definition: Methods that involve crossing disciplinary boundaries to address sustainability issues, often through collaboration between academics and non-academic stakeholders, fostering holistic understanding and novel problem-solving.
evidence: [TayLea_2021] we explore interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary learning, reflective thinking, and experiential learning.
[KerUNE_2020] initiated the integration of transdisciplinary approaches into partner universities.

themes.name: Sustainability Competencies and Learning Outcomes
themes.definition: The specific skills, knowledge, and abilities that students are expected to develop through Education for Sustainable Development, often defined through competency models and assessed via learning objectives.
evidence: [SánEdu_2021] The questionnaire consists of 18 questions concerning four sustainability competencies: C1-Critical contextualization of knowledge, C2-Sustainable use of resources, C3-Participation in community processes, and C4-Ethics.
[WilImp_2019] the need for integration of competences in tertiary education for sustainable development (ESD).

themes.name: Barriers to ESD Implementation
themes.definition: Challenges and obstacles faced in integrating Education for Sustainable Development into higher education, such as lack of funding, inadequate training, conceptual confusion, or institutional resistance.
evidence: [CavPro_2021] the HEIs surveyed still have not developed enough work to distinguish conceptually between sustainable development, ESD and SL making the embedment of these concepts in the curriculum not fully developed.
[Sá Uni_2020] Universities face many barriers including lack of funding, not properly trained people and inept government policies.

themes.name: Student Perspectives and Engagement
themes.definition: Focusing on students' perceptions, motivations, and active involvement in sustainability, including their knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and self-efficacy beliefs, often assessed through surveys and interviews.
evidence: [SanDo _2020] This study aimed to analyze students of Universidad Autónoma de Madrid (UAM), focusing on their attitudes, behaviors, and level of knowledge concerning education for sustainable development (ESD).
[Obe“I _2021] explores their study choice motives as well as sustainability-related conceptions, engagement and self-efficacy beliefs.

themes.name: Tools and Frameworks for ESD
themes.definition: The use of specific models, instruments, or frameworks to guide, assess, or implement Education for Sustainable Development, such as UNESCO frameworks, assessment tools, or pedagogical models.
evidence: [KerUNE_2020] uses the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) framework for Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) beyond 2019 to reflect on the CaucaSusT project.
[CaeSus_2020] critically reflect the existing tools to assess and benchmark ESD implementation.

data.meta_observations: The abstracts frequently emphasize assessment methods (e.g., surveys, scales) and competency-based approaches, with a strong focus on both student and educator perspectives. Institutional strategies and barriers are commonly discussed, indicating a recognition of systemic challenges. Pedagogical innovations like interdisciplinary and design-thinking are highlighted as effective for ESD. Many studies are context-specific, focusing on particular countries or regions.
data.grounding_notes: Some abstracts have quality issues (e.g., missing results, no quantitative data) as noted, but only explicit statements were used for evidence. Themes were derived inductively from verbatim text, and all article keys are from the provided closed set. Confidence is high for all themes due to clear evidence across multiple abstracts.
